learning: FIRST CAPTURE-RATE MEASUREMENTS. Four replies from 2026-09-24: MarkMinervini 785 impressions on 14,047 target views = 5.59%; EliteOptions2 94 on 12,443 = 0.76%; MapleStax 7 on 2,027 = 0.35%; CKCapitalxx 17 on 14,982 = 0.11%. Ordering capture by the two candidate drivers is decisive in one direction and negative in the other. By views-per-minute the order is Minervini 1277, EliteOptions2 389, CKCapitalxx 113, MapleStax 97 - which reproduces the capture ordering almost exactly (only the bottom two, which are 16% apart in velocity, swap). By fewest existing replies the order is MapleStax 2, Minervini 4, EliteOptions2 8, CKCapitalxx 9 - and MapleStax, the LEAST crowded thread of the four, finished second worst. So the primary clause of the crowding rule (rank by views-per-minute) is supported, while the secondary clause (then by fewest replies) is not: thread crowding did not separate these four, post velocity did. The likely mechanism is that reply count and absolute reach are confounded - a thread with almost no replies usually has almost no readers - so 'uncrowded' is only valuable when the post is also travelling. Practical revision to test next: rank on views-per-minute alone and use the ~50-reply figure purely as a veto on obviously buried threads, rather than as a positive ranking term. This is n=4 on a single day against the account's n>=5 and >=2x bar, so it stays a hypothesis - but the 51x spread between best and worst is far beyond the 2x threshold and the top result is a single creator, so the more urgent caveat is that MarkMinervini may simply be a better target than the others rather than early arrival being what worked. Next run should reply to Minervini early again and to one other creator at comparable velocity; if Minervini repeats near 5% and the other does not, the driver is the creator, not the timing.
